record.original_question: Let v be a continuous viscosity supersolution of the local complex Monge-Ampere equation -(dd^c V)^n + f dV = 0 on a bounded domain. If P(v) denotes the plurisubharmonic envelope of v, determine whether P(v) is a pluripotential supersolution of the same equation.

evidence.quote: Question 40 (Eyssidieux-Guedj-Zeriahi). Let v be a continuous viscosity supersolution of the equation -(dd^c V)^n + f dV = 0. Is P(v) a pluripotential supersolution of the same equation ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded domain, and let $f \geq 0$ be a continuous function on $\Omega$. Consider the local complex Monge–Ampère equation
$$-(dd^c V)^n + f\, dV = 0,$$
where $dV$ denotes Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{C}^n$ and $(dd^c V)^n$ is interpreted in the appropriate (viscosity or pluripotential) sense.

Recall:
- A continuous function $v: \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ is a viscosity supersolution of the equation if, at every point $x_0 \in \Omega$ and for every $C^2$ test function $q$ touching $v$ from below at $x_0$, one has $-(dd^c q(x_0))^n + f(x_0)\, dV \geq 0$ in the viscosity sense (i.e., either $dd^c q(x_0)$ is not positive semidefinite, or $(dd^c q(x_0))^n \leq f(x_0)\, dV$).
- The plurisubharmonic envelope of $v$ is defined by
$$P(v)(z) := \sup\{ u(z) : u \text{ plurisubharmonic on } \Omega,\ u \leq v \text{ on } \Omega \}.$$
- A plurisubharmonic function $u$ is a pluripotential supersolution of the equation if the Monge–Ampère measure $(dd^c u)^n$ (in the sense of Bedford–Taylor, when defined) satisfies $(dd^c u)^n \leq f\, dV$.

Question: Given a continuous viscosity supersolution $v$ of $-(dd^c V)^n + f\, dV = 0$ on $\Omega$, is $P(v)$ a pluripotential supersolution of the same equation?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears to be answered affirmatively in the paper "Plurisubharmonic envelopes and supersolutions" by Lu, Phạm, and others (J. Differential Geom., 2019), whose abstract states: "We show that the quasi-plurisubharmonic envelope of a viscosity super-solution is a pluripotential super-solution of a given complex Monge–Ampère equation." This establishes the result on both compact Kähler manifolds and domains in $\mathbb{C}^n$.

status_evidence.title: Plurisubharmonic envelopes and supersolutions
status_evidence.snippet: We show that the quasi-plurisubharmonic envelope of a viscosity super-solution is a pluripotential super-solution of a given complex Monge–Ampère equation.
status_evidence.claim: The plurisubharmonic envelope of a (viscosity) supersolution of the complex Monge–Ampère equation is a pluripotential supersolution, answering the question affirmatively.
